correctness.rationale: From the simultaneous row update in RESULT.md:17–27, all rows grow and the set A of worlds with no a-successor outside P shrinks. If a nonempty A is unchanged by an update, all rows of all agents meet that same set after the update, so the following update is the identity; if A is empty, the update is the identity immediately. Count at most |A_0| strict decreases if A reaches the empty set, or at most |A_0|-1 strict decreases plus one strict constant-set round otherwise. A survivor while A contains a false-p world cannot have previously gained an edge, since every earlier A contained that same world and receiving it would have expelled the survivor permanently. Testing its original row against the current A therefore gives precisely the sink-deletion rule. The directed path pointing toward its terminal sink starts with A=W, loses exactly one vertex from the right until all are lost, and includes the one-world empty-row case. Propositional truth sets are fixed by the edge update on any carrier, so the update is idempotent. The finite bitmask checks in verify.py are consistent in scope; inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: No extension of the finite n-bound to infinite carriers, arbitrary modal formulas, or other event-update semantics is certified.
